question.text: Mr. Deepak Iyer, Manager of Vindhya Debt Opportunities (Cat II AIF), wishes to invest in Security Receipts issued by an ARC. Which of the following investments is EXPRESSLY PROHIBITED under the SARFAESI / AIF framework due to conflict of interest?

answer.text: Investing in SRs backed by stressed loans of an unrelated mid-cap textile company
Investing in SRs rated below investment grade by CRISIL
Investing in SRs issued by an ARC that happens to be the fund's portfolio investee company
Investing in SRs denominated in foreign currency

explanation.text: The Logic: Per p.263, an AIF cannot invest in SRs issued by an ARC that is its portfolio investee company, and cannot invest in SRs backed by underlying loans of its associate or group companies — both are conflict-of-interest prohibitions. Per p.533, AIFs are recognised as Qualified Buyers permitted to subscribe to SRs issued by ARCs, subject to such restrictions. The Trap: SRs backed by stressed loans of an unrelated company, the credit rating of the SR, and foreign-currency denomination are not flagged in the checked pages as the express conflict-of-interest prohibition the question asks about. Note: The express prohibition arises specifically where the AIF's investee/associate/group relationship creates the conflict, as set out on p.263.
